tip: hoe de vork in de steel zit literally means how the fork sits in its handle, and stands for how things really are.
slagen in becomes erin slagen, where er points ahead to what you succeed in: Zij slaagt erin om alles klaar te krijgen = she manages to get it done.
om te plus an infinitive marks purpose, in order to: om te studeren = in order to study.
om de hete brij draaien literally means to circle around the hot porridge, and means to beat around the bush.
met de mond vol tanden staan literally means to stand with your mouth full of teeth, and means to be lost for words.
met de handen in het haar zitten literally means to sit with your hands in your hair, and means to be at your wits end.
A whole clause can fill first position, and the finite verb still comes right after it: Hoe dat precies is gebeurd, heeft niemand, with heeft before the subject niemand.
zin hebben om plus te plus an infinitive means to feel like doing something: heb je zin om langs te komen = do you feel like coming over.
Fronting niet alleen puts the verb before the subject: Niet alleen spreekt zij, just like English Not only does she speak.
A question word plus ook means no matter: Hoeveel het ook kost = no matter how much it costs, same pattern as hoe dan ook.
vergane glorie is a set phrase for bygone or faded glory, used of things past their prime.
laten plus zich plus an infinitive means can or cannot be done: de waarheid laat zich niet vangen = the truth cannot be captured.
The fronted clause Pas als de zon schijnt pushes the verb ahead of the subject: komen de toeristen, not de toeristen komen. English keeps the subject first.
Hoe plus a comparative twice means the more, the more: Hoe langer, hoe moeilijker, and both verbs go to the end, wacht and wordt.
steeds plus a comparative means more and more: steeds warmer = warmer and warmer, increasingly warm.
Fronting Nauwelijks flips the verb before the subject: Nauwelijks waren we aangekomen, just like English Hardly had we arrived.
dienen te is a formal, official must or should: dient te worden verhoogd = must be raised.
der is an archaic genitive meaning of the: de vlam der hoop = the flame of hope; modern Dutch says van de.
dat hoort zo literally means that belongs so, and is used for that is how it should be or that is proper.
wiens is the relative whose for a masculine or neuter antecedent: de visser wiens verhalen = the fisherman whose stories.
der in de loop der tijd is a fossilized genitive meaning of the, kept only in fixed phrases; it means over the course of time.
zij in het zij zo is the old subjunctive of zijn, meaning so be it; the same zij appears in God zij dank.
zo plus dat frames a result: zo dicht langs elkaar dat je de gesprekken kunt volgen = so close that you can follow them.
Indien is the formal, written word for if, where als is the everyday spoken one: Indien de omstandigheden het toelaten = if circumstances permit.
hoe plus ook means however or no matter how: Hoe onwaarschijnlijk het ook mag klinken = however unlikely it may sound.
